from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout
        lines = [
            "Meet Leo, our feline friend on a 2D grid.",
            "Matrices transform space, stretching and squashing everything inside.",
            "Watch Leo distort as we apply a linear transformation.",
            "Most points shift to entirely new directions.",
            "But some special lines stay fixed in their orientation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite & The Core Intuition", lines)

        # Matrix for transformation: [[2, 0.5], [0, 1]]
        matrix = [[2, 0.5], [0, 1]]

        # Helper to create Leo the Cat
        def get_leo():
            head = Circle(radius=0.6, color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.3)
            # Ears
            ear_l = Polygon([-0.5, 0.4, 0], [-0.2, 0.5, 0], [-0.6, 0.9, 0], color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.5)
            ear_r = Polygon([0.5, 0.4, 0], [0.2, 0.5, 0], [0.6, 0.9, 0], color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=0.5)
            # Eyes
            eye_l = Dot([-0.2, 0.2, 0], radius=0.05, color="#FFFF00")
            eye_r = Dot([0.2, 0.2, 0], radius=0.05, color="#FFFF00")
            # Mouth/Nose
            nose = Triangle(color="#FFFF00", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.05).move_to([0, 0, 0])
            # Whiskers
            w1 = Line([-0.7, 0.1, 0], [-0.2, 0, 0], color="#FFFF00")
            w2 = Line([-0.7, -0.1, 0], [-0.2, 0, 0], color="#FFFF00")
            w3 = Line([0.7, 0.1, 0], [0.2, 0, 0], color="#FFFF00")
            w4 = Line([0.7, -0.1, 0], [0.2, 0, 0], color="#FFFF00")
            return VGroup(head, ear_l, ear_r, eye_l, eye_r, nose, w1, w2, w3, w4)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Grid area
        grid_visual = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1], y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#FFFFFF", "stroke_width": 1, "stroke_opacity": 0.5}
        ).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(grid_visual, 'A1', 'F6')
        
        leo = get_leo().scale(0.5)
        leo.move_to(grid_visual.c2p(0, 0))
        
        self.play(Create(grid_visual), FadeIn(leo))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Add vectors before transformation
        v_green = Arrow(grid_visual.c2p(0,0), grid_visual.c2p(1,0), color="#00FF00", buff=0, stroke_width=4)
        v_red = Arrow(grid_visual.c2p(0,0), grid_visual.c2p(1,1), color="#FF0000", buff=0, stroke_width=4)
        
        matrix_label = Text("A = [[2, 0.5], [0, 1]]", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(matrix_label, 'A6')

        self.play(GrowArrow(v_green), GrowArrow(v_red), Write(matrix_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Transform the grid, leo, and vectors
        # Note: Manim's apply_matrix is a coordinate transform. 
        # For simplicity in this layout, we animate the points' movement.
        
        new_v_green_end = grid_visual.c2p(2, 0) # [1,0] * A = [2,0]
        new_v_red_end = grid_visual.c2p(2.5, 1) # [1,1] * A = [2.5, 1]
        
        self.play(
            grid_visual.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),
            leo.animate.apply_matrix(matrix),
            v_green.animate.put_start_and_end_on(grid_visual.c2p(0,0), new_v_green_end),
            v_red.animate.put_start_and_end_on(grid_visual.c2p(0,0), new_v_red_end),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(RED)
        
        # Highlight red vector changing direction
        flash_red = v_red.copy().set_color(WHITE).set_stroke(width=6)
        self.play(FadeIn(flash_red), ScaleInPlace(flash_red, 1.2))
        self.play(FadeOut(flash_red))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(GREEN)
        
        # Highlight green vector staying on line
        eigen_label = Text("Eigen-direction", font_size=18, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(eigen_label, 'E6')
        
        # Draw a dotted line to show the original span
        span_line = DashedLine(grid_visual.c2p(-3,0), grid_visual.c2p(3,0), color="#00FF00", stroke_opacity=0.5)
        
        self.play(Create(span_line), Write(eigen_label))
        self.play(Indicate(v_green, color="#00FF00"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup layout with specific title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout(
            "Defining the Eigen-Relationship", 
            [
                "The relationship is defined as A v equals lambda v.", 
                "The eigenvector v stays on its original line.", 
                "The eigenvalue lambda scales that vector's length."
            ]
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Equation: A v = λ v
        # Characters: [0]:A, [1]:v, [2]:'=', [3]:λ, [4]:v
        eqn = VGroup(
            Text("A"), Text("v"), Text("="), Text("λ"), Text("v")
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        # Initial state: White
        eqn.set_color(WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(eqn, "B1", "B6", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
            Write(eqn),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Logic: Highlight A (Blue) and λ (Gold). 
        # Show a vector v (Green) on its line (span).
        
        span_line = Line(
            start=self.grid["E1"], 
            end=self.grid["E6"], 
            color=GRAY, 
            stroke_opacity=0.3
        )
        
        # Vector v starting at E2 and pointing to E3
        v_start = self.grid["E2"]
        v_end = self.grid["E3"]
        vector_v = Arrow(
            start=v_start, 
            end=v_end, 
            buff=0, 
            color="#00FF00", 
            stroke_width=6
        )
        v_label = Text("v", color="#00FF00", font_size=20).next_to(vector_v, UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"),
            eqn[0].animate.set_color("#0000FF"), # Matrix A to Blue
            eqn[3].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), # Lambda to Gold
            Create(span_line),
            GrowArrow(vector_v),
            FadeIn(v_label),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Logic: Animate the green vector 'v' scaling by factor 3.
        
        # Target end point (E2 + 3 units right = E5)
        v_end_scaled = self.grid["E5"]
        vector_v_scaled = Arrow(
            start=v_start, 
            end=v_end_scaled, 
            buff=0, 
            color="#00FF00", 
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        # Also update label position relative to new vector
        v_label_target = Text("3v", color="#FFD700", font_size=20).next_to(vector_v_scaled, UP, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFD700"),
            Transform(vector_v, vector_v_scaled),
            Transform(v_label, v_label_target),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup title and lecture lines
        title_str = "The Characteristic Equation (The Math Tool)"
        lines = [
            "To find these values, we rewrite the equation.",
            "Set the determinant of A minus lambda I to zero.",
            "This condition ensures non-zero solutions for our vectors."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Transition: 'A v = λ v' to '(A - λ I) v = 0'
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Build A v = lambda v
        eq1 = VGroup(
            Text("A", color=WHITE),
            Text("v", color=WHITE),
            Text(" = ", color=WHITE),
            Text("\u03BB", color=WHITE),
            Text("v", color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(eq1, "A2", "B5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(eq1))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Build (A - lambda I) v = 0
        eq2 = VGroup(
            Text("(", color=WHITE),
            Text("A", color=WHITE),
            Text(" - ", color=WHITE),
            Text("\u03BB", color=WHITE),
            Text("I", color=WHITE),
            Text(")", color=WHITE),
            Text("v", color=WHITE),
            Text(" = ", color=WHITE),
            Text("0", color=WHITE)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(eq2, "A2", "B5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Transition
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(eq1, eq2))
        
        # Highlight (A - lambda I) with a red box
        # Red box around the "(A - lambda I)" part (indices 0 to 5)
        red_box = SurroundingRectangle(eq2[:6], color="#FF0000", buff=0.1)
        self.play(Create(red_box))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Display text 'Matrix must be singular for non-zero v' (#FFFFFF)
        singular_text = Text("Matrix must be singular for non-zero v", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(singular_text, "C1", "C6", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(singular_text))
        
        # Write 'det(A - λ I) = 0' in yellow (#FFFF00)
        det_eq = VGroup(
            Text("det", color=YELLOW),
            Text("(", color=YELLOW),
            Text("A", color=YELLOW),
            Text(" - ", color=YELLOW),
            Text("\u03BB", color=YELLOW),
            Text("I", color=YELLOW),
            Text(")", color=YELLOW),
            Text(" = ", color=YELLOW),
            Text("0", color=YELLOW)
        ).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(det_eq, "D1", "D6", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(det_eq))
        
        # Glowing emphasis (using Flash or temporary highlight)
        self.play(Indicate(det_eq, color=YELLOW, scale_factor=1.1))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700") # Gold
        
        # Show a 2x2 matrix with 'λ' subtracted from diagonal elements in gold (#FFD700)
        # Components of the matrix
        b_left = Text("[", font_size=80, color="#FFD700")
        b_right = Text("]", font_size=80, color="#FFD700")
        
        # Elements
        a_minus_lam = Text("a - \u03BB", color="#FFD700", font_size=32)
        b_elem = Text("b", color="#FFD700", font_size=32)
        c_elem = Text("c", color="#FFD700", font_size=32)
        d_minus_lam = Text("d - \u03BB", color="#FFD700", font_size=32)
        
        # Layout
        row1 = VGroup(a_minus_lam, b_elem).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.2)
        row2 = VGroup(c_elem, d_minus_lam).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.2)
        
        # Align columns
        a_minus_lam.align_to(c_elem, LEFT)
        b_elem.align_to(d_minus_lam, LEFT)
        
        elements = VGroup(row1, row2).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.6)
        matrix_vgroup = VGroup(b_left, elements, b_right).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        self.place_in_area(matrix_vgroup, "E1", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_vgroup))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with lecture lines
        lecture_lines = [
            "Let's calculate the eigenvalues for this specific matrix.", 
            "Subtract lambda from the diagonal elements.", 
            "Calculate the determinant to get a quadratic equation.", 
            "Solve for lambda to find our two scaling factors.", 
            "Here, our eigenvalues are five and two."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Step-by-Step Calculation Example", lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Matrix A = [[4, 1], [2, 3]]
        m_4 = Text("4", font_size=36)
        m_1 = Text("1", font_size=36)
        m_2 = Text("2", font_size=36)
        m_3 = Text("3", font_size=36)
        
        vals_row1 = VGroup(m_4, m_1).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.2)
        vals_row2 = VGroup(m_2, m_3).arrange(RIGHT, buff=1.2)
        matrix_vals = VGroup(vals_row1, vals_row2).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.8)
        
        l_bracket = Text("[", font_size=100)
        r_bracket = Text("]", font_size=100)
        matrix_full = VGroup(l_bracket, matrix_vals, r_bracket).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        
        a_label = Text("A =", font_size=36)
        matrix_disp = VGroup(a_label, matrix_full).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        # Place in B-C area
        self.place_in_area(matrix_disp, "B1", "C6")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(matrix_disp))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        
        # Prepare for determinant det(A - λI) = 0
        l_bar = Text("|", font_size=100)
        r_bar = Text("|", font_size=100)
        m_4_sub = Text("4 - \u03BB", font_size=30)
        m_3_sub = Text("3 - \u03BB", font_size=30)
        
        # Grouping for determinant
        det_vals_row1 = VGroup(m_4_sub, m_1.copy()).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)
        det_vals_row2 = VGroup(m_2.copy(), m_3_sub).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.8)
        det_vals = VGroup(det_vals_row1, det_vals_row2).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.8)
        
        det_full = VGroup(l_bar, det_vals, r_bar).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.2)
        det_eq = Text("= 0", font_size=36)
        det_disp = VGroup(det_full, det_eq).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        
        # Place in same area as matrix
        self.place_in_area(det_disp, "B1", "C6")

        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)

        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

outline.topic: Eigenvalues of 2x2 Matrices: The DNA of Linear Transformations
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in STEM fields (Mathematics, Physics, Engineering)

sections.title: Prerequisite & The Core Intuition
sections.content: Start by reviewing a 2x2 matrix as a 'transformer' of 2D space. Introduce 'Leo the Linear Cat,' a character drawn on a 2D grid. When we multiply the grid by a matrix, Leo gets stretched or squashed. Explain that while most points on Leo move to brand new directions, certain 'special' directions stay fixed along their original lines.
sections.example: Visualize Leo the Cat on a grid. Apply a transformation where he is stretched horizontally by 2. His whiskers on the x-axis stay on the x-axis (eigen-direction), while whiskers at 45 degrees tilt toward the horizontal.

sections.title: Defining the Eigen-Relationship
sections.content: Introduce the fundamental equation: Av = λv. Explain that 'A' is the matrix, 'v' is the eigenvector (the direction that doesn't change), and 'λ' (lambda) is the eigenvalue (the scale factor). Emphasize that in this specific direction, matrix multiplication simplifies to simple scalar multiplication.
sections.example: If A maps a vector v to 3v, then λ = 3. This means the 'DNA' of this transformation in that direction is a growth factor of 3.

sections.title: The Characteristic Equation (The Math Tool)
sections.content: Transition from geometry to algebra. To solve Av = λv, we rewrite it as (A - λI)v = 0. Explain that for a non-zero vector 'v' to exist, the matrix (A - λI) must be 'singular,' meaning its determinant must be zero. This leads to the characteristic equation: det(A - λI) = 0.
sections.example: Show a 2x2 matrix with 'λ' subtracted from the top-left and bottom-right diagonal elements, preparing it for the determinant calculation.

sections.title: Step-by-Step Calculation Example
sections.content: Walk through a concrete calculation using a 2x2 matrix. Show the expansion of the determinant into a quadratic equation (the characteristic polynomial) and solve for λ using factoring or the quadratic formula.
sections.example: Matrix A = [[4, 1], [2, 3]]. Calculation: det([[4-λ, 1], [2, 3-λ]]) = (4-λ)(3-λ) - 2 = λ² - 7λ + 10 = 0. Solving (λ-5)(λ-2)=0 gives eigenvalues λ₁=5 and λ₂=2.

sections.title: Visualizing the Resulting Transformation
sections.content: Connect the math back to Leo the Cat. Explain what the specific eigenvalues mean for the shape. If λ > 1, space expands; if 0 < λ < 1, space compresses; if λ is negative, space flips.
sections.example: Animate Leo being stretched 5 times longer along one diagonal (λ=5) and 2 times longer along another (λ=2). This gives a complete 'physical profile' of how the matrix A behaves.

sections.title: Summary & Application
sections.content: Wrap up by highlighting that eigenvalues are used in everything from Google's PageRank algorithm to analyzing the vibration of bridge cables. Reinforce that eigenvalues represent the 'scaling power' of a transformation.
sections.example: A bridge (device) vibrating: its 'natural frequencies' are determined by the eigenvalues of its structural matrix. High eigenvalue = high frequency vibration.
